text: The boy on Fifth Avenue used to trot and canter!” “Do you think you could trot and canter?” said the Earl. “I should like to try,” answered Fauntleroy. His lordship made a sign to Wilkins, who at the signal brought up his own horse and mounted it and took Fauntleroy's pony by the leading-rein. “Now,” said the Earl, “let him trot.” The next few minutes were rather exciting to the small equestrian. He found that trotting was not so easy as walking, and the faster the pony trotted, the less easy it was.
